**Order: (1) the inner-box clamp (D.8) on the offset, then (2) the limits clamp on the pose; the limits win.** `c_1 = target + clamp(d + L, −B, +B)` (D.8; in the D.6b variant the offset form `o`); `[lo, hi] = [rect_eff.min + field/2, rect_eff.max − field/2]` per axis (`lo = hi = rect_eff` centre on an axis where `field` is larger than the rect, C8); **`c = clamp(c_1, lo, hi)`** per axis, then quantisation (D.9). **The clamp acts on the pose, not on the follow target**, so `f` and the cut predicates never see it (reconciliation 4 stands) and the aim mapping's `f_q` is unaffected. In a static rect this is continuous: walking into a wall slows the pose to a stop at `hi` with no pop (the unclamped pose crosses `hi` continuously). **A change of the rect never pops the pose**: the solver keeps an eased copy `rect_eff` whose four edges approach the `PROJECTOR`'s rect with the D.6 factor (`rect_eff ← rect_eff + a·(rect − rect_eff)`, settle at `SETTLE_EPS`), so a pose that falls outside the new rect is carried to its edge along the same exponential — `t_95 = 3·τ_follow_eff` = 0.54 s, zero overshoot — and `rect_eff` snaps to the rect on a `CUT`, on a `RESCALING` frame (a zoom step is a cut by C6) and on load. **`CLAMPED` suspends the 60 % guarantee** on the clamped axis: with the avatar near a hull edge the clamped centre can sit up to `field/2` from it, so the avatar may leave the central 60 % (D.8's `|c − target| ≤ B` holds only while `FOLLOWING`); it stays inside the picture because the avatar is inside the rect, and no prompt is drawn outside the picture (C9). `diag.limits_engaged` records the axis and frames.

findings.finding: The rewritten S oracle fires too early. The AC says that 'once the follow lag has settled (>= 3*tau_eff = 0.54 s)' S 'equals floor(-(lag_ss(dt) + (1 - alpha_draw)*3)) on every frame'. A first-order follow from rest has residual lag_ss*e^(-3), about 5 %, at 3*tau. That is about 1.5 px at v_run, and the GDD's own settle clause (L788) says 0.75 s is needed just to get within SETTLE_EPS = 0.5 px. At 60 fps, S at t = 0.54 s is floor(-33.75 + 1.5) = -33, not the asserted -34. At 144 fps the margin for {-34.8..-32.05} is under 0.05 px, so even 0.75 s is not enough. A correct implementation fails this (auto) AC, the same defect class as the previous blocker (G4).
findings.fix: Change the settle precondition in the AC (and the matching D.14b / PC fixture text) to >= 10*tau_eff = 1.8 s, where residual is at most 0.0014 of the lag, or to a stated residual bound (lag within 0.02 px of lag_ss). Player Controller PC-5, the f_q variable row, the cursor-held-still edge case, AC-PCI-056 (its running fixture recomputed from atan2 as aim_q 1637 and verified) and AC-PCI-059 mirror the bound. Registry aim_shift_S exists with referenced_by set.

RESOLVED: earlier G4 blocker, D.3 residual with the cap bound. 3440x1440, 1280x800, 1600x900, 1366x768, 1365x768, 2560x1080 and 3840x1080 re-computed to (860,360), (640,400), (800,450), (682,384), (682,384), (852,360), (960,360) with residual bars 0/0, 1/1, 0/1, 2/2, 480/480. The AC and the D.3 prose agree.

RESOLVED: earlier G4 blocker, D.15 Y_scale floor. The 0.0355/0.0400 and 0.00/0.04 fixtures and the 0.50 -> 0.59 -> 0.50 pair re-check against the formula (F = 0, F = 2, F = 0 frame-mean, F = 1 single light).

PARTLY RESOLVED: earlier G4 blocker, 'never twice in a frame'. It is now scoped to f_render >= 60 and the frame-step AC (L1032) is correct for a 1 px/tick body. The promise sentences (PR-4 rule 3, PR-11 row 144, D.17, Game Feel) still read as general and are false at the shipped speeds (see RECOMMENDED finding).

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria > Camera follow, look-ahead, cuts (mouse-aim AC, L1060); Formulas D.14b fixtures
findings.finding: The rewritten S oracle fires too early. The AC says that 'once the follow lag has settled (>= 3*tau_eff = 0.54 s)' S 'equals floor(-(lag_ss(dt) + (1 - alpha_draw)*3)) on every frame'. A first-order follow from rest has residual lag_ss*e^(-3), about 5 %, at 3*tau. That is about 1.5 px at v_run, and the GDD's own settle clause (L788) says 0.75 s is needed just to get within SETTLE_EPS = 0.5 px. At 60 fps, S at t = 0.54 s is floor(-33.75 + 1.5) = -33, not the asserted -34. At 144 fps the margin for {-34.8..-32.05} is under 0.05 px, so even 0.75 s is not enough. A correct implementation fails this (auto) AC, the same defect class as the previous blocker (G4).
findings.fix: Change the settle precondition in the AC (and the matching D.14b / PC fixture text) to >= 10*tau_eff = 1.8 s, where residual is at most 0.0014 of the lag, or to a stated residual bound (lag within 0.02 px of lag_ss). Keep the 3*tau_eff figure only for the t_95 claim. If equality at 0.75 s is wanted instead, relax the oracle to 'within 2 base px'.

findings.section: Core Rules PR-4 rule 3 (L119), PR-11 row 144 (L221), D.17 Output Range (L729), Game Feel
findings.finding: The scoped promise 'base-pixel steps ... never twice in a frame at f_render >= 60' is still false at the speeds the game ships. v_walk = 2 px/tick at 90 fps steps 1 or 2 px per frame; v_run = 3 px/tick at 144 fps (1.25 px/frame) steps 1 or 2, at 90 fps exactly 2, at 60 fps 3. D.17's own line 'at v_run ... >= 1 px every frame' contradicts the promise. The fix pass scoped the frame rate but not the speed; only the AC (L1032) states the 1 px/tick premise. Spike step 12 'measures it' with real speeds and would fail.
findings.fix: Restate the promise everywhere as: per-frame step = ticks committed in the frame times px/tick, at most ceil(v/f_render) base px, never backward, whole base px only. 'Never twice' stays only as the 1 px/tick fixture statement.

findings.finding: Two issues. (a) D.6b is still headed 'default candidate' (also C3 L162 and OQ 12) although the creative-director's earlier call made it the normative MVP solver; the story has no single normative solver. (b) On the D.6b path pose_q is floored first and the limits clamp is applied afterwards against the eased float rect_eff, while D.8b says clamp then quantise. During a rect ease (detach, weld) the camera pose can be non-integer, violating PR-4 rule 2 and the whole-base-px rule.
findings.fix: Declare D.6b normative and D.6/D.9 the fallback. On the D.6b path apply the limits clamp to the unquantised pose then floor(), or floor rect_eff per axis (integer lo/hi); add an AC for an integer pose on every frame of a rect ease.

findings.section: D.12 entity_id (L581), PR-5, OQ 27(b); registry layout_entity_id_namespace; Layout OQ-33
findings.finding: Deadlock on the namespace surface. Pipeline D.12 says 'each other publisher registers its namespace tag with this GDD', while Layout and the registry say LAYOUT_ID_NS is 'to be agreed with the Pipeline owner'. No tag table exists, and the actor publisher's 'tagged form of Body's block-local actor_id' has no formula. Actors and horrors share class_rank 3 with small per-block counters, so the globally-unique-id claim and the collision fallback 'order by (publisher namespace tag, tree order)' cannot be implemented. Under G6 this GAP is the owner's to fill.
findings.fix: Add a namespace table in D.12: tag byte per publisher (Layout, Body actors, Horror, Interaction, others), the 56-bit-shift layout for Body and Horror ids, and the rule that class_rank 2 items sort by entity_id alone. Update the registry entry and add the Pipeline to its referenced_by.

findings.section: D.14b / D.8b / OQ 18 (CLAMPED aim mismatch)
findings.finding: While the camera is CLAMPED, f_q can sit up to field/2 (D.8b's own example: 140+ px) from the clamped picture, so a hidden-cursor mouse aim is measured against a pose that is not what the player sees. The lamp is the core verb. The mismatch is unbounded and no AC or playtest metric covers it (OQ 18 mentions only the follow lag).
findings.fix: State the bound in D.14b (|f_q - clamped pose| <= field/2 on a clamped axis), add it to the OQ 18 playtest item (hull-edge aiming) and add an AC that the aim at a clamped axis equals the formula; or decide to publish a clamp-aware anchor.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria evidence classes (header L999, L1062, L1063, Performance L1171-1183, Gaps)
findings.finding: Four problems. (1) '(auto, in-engine)' on the cursor-unit AC (L1062) is not a defined class; the header limits (auto) to headless pure functions, and this AC needs a real window, so it should be (manual) or a windowed-runner class. (2) The six performance ACs (L1173-1182, except the frame-time one marked (manual)) have no class tag. (3) L1063 'neither story is marked ready until the previous AC is passing' is a process gate, not pass/fail. (4) The Gaps bullet 'Performance figures are unsourced ... a miss logs, it does not fail' contradicts the R12 gating (P99 <= 90 % of ceiling, a miss withholds a zoom step).
findings.fix: Tag L1062 (manual; windowed run, retained capture) and the performance ACs '(manual; pending spike on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK)'. Move L1063 into Open Question 28 as a /story-readiness precondition. Rewrite the Gaps bullet to the R12 wording.

findings.section: PR-15 / Startup assertions ACs (L1156-1161) vs PR-7
findings.finding: The project.godot parse AC and the startup read-back hard-code stretch mode 'canvas_items' and scale_mode 'integer', while PR-7 and OQ 1 leave wiring (i) open (the leading candidate). A correct wiring-(i) build fails the (auto) AC. The cursor-unit AC is correctly wiring-agnostic.
findings.fix: Parametrise: 'the stretch keys required by the chosen wiring (table of keys per wiring (i)/(ii))', or gate these keys on the render-pipeline ADR.

findings.section: Spike gating (D intro L322, AC header, Gaps) vs art bible 8.12
findings.finding: About ten rules and ACs are gated on 'steps 11 stretch and window, 12 motion integrity, 13 pacing', which are the engine-programmer's proposed steps. Art bible 8.12 has no steps 11-13 (checked), so a producer has nothing to schedule. This is a carry-over; the fix pass did not touch it.
findings.fix: Route an art-bible 8.12 amendment adding steps 11-13 with owner and pass line, or restate the gates as a pipeline-owned spike list in this GDD (Open Question) and schedule it.

findings.section: Sibling GDDs: Web Map & Transit (OQ-WM-25, AC-WM-115, G-8); Player Controller (D.7b hand-off L532, OQ 30(a) L1396)
findings.finding: Two sibling conformance gaps. (a) Pipeline OQ 16 (R21) holds the berth Settle to VS-A and says Web Map 'conforms: no MVP camera Settle', but Web Map still lists OQ-WM-25 as open ('agent (Pipeline owner), next GDD') and AC-WM-115 as an MVP (manual, Visual) criterion that peaks at 2 art px. It cannot pass with JOLT_MAX = 0. (b) Player Controller D.7b and its OQ 30(a) still ask the Pipeline to move the run weight off a smoothstep on |v|, but the Pipeline already keys on loco_state == RUN plus octant (D.7, L469), so this is stale.
findings.fix: Web Map: close OQ-WM-25 per R21 and re-tag AC-WM-115 as VS-A / waived. Player Controller: rewrite the D.7b hand-off and OQ 30(a) as done, keep only the 'safe range starts at 0.50' note.

findings.section: Stale text and counts (L22, L30, L168, L889, L1235(e); registry)
findings.finding: Stale items remain. (1) Quick reference L22 and Overview L30 say '17 downstream dependents' while Dependencies counts 22 (17 + rows 18-22). (2) C6 L168 says 'user ratification pending - Open Question 4' but OQ 4 is RESOLVED by user decision. (3) L889 and OQ 27(e) still say registry entries are 'requested, not edited here' though follow_offset_quantised, limits_clamp, ZOOM_MIN_K and the min(1,s) text have landed. (4) Registry referenced_by is empty for mouse_to_world_aim, follow_offset_quantised, limits_clamp and layout_entity_id_namespace although Player Controller and Layout cite them; registry L7480 carries an old 'FOLLOW_TAU * s' comment. (5) The systems index still lists the pipeline as 'Needs Revision' and lacks the Interactions rows 9, 13-22.
findings.fix: Update counts to 22 (or '17 + 5'); rewrite L168 as 'resolved'; change 'requested' to 'landed 2026-10-27'; populate referenced_by lists; refresh the index.

findings.section: Dependencies (rows for cite-only consumers; Settings rows)
findings.finding: Item & Module Database (3 citations), Sanity & Hallucination Rules (2), Life-Support Graph and Boarding & Salvage (0) are not listed, and Life-Support and Boarding do not cite the pipeline at all. The bidirectional rule is unmet for them, though they are cite-only consumers. The Settings & Accessibility rows say 'Not yet written (Alpha)' instead of R9's 'undesigned - provisional contract' with the assumed interface.
findings.fix: Add soft cite-only rows (or a sentence stating the exclusion) and relabel the two Settings rows 'undesigned - provisional contract: PR-14 option set, integer step sets'.

findings.section: AC L1060 fixture / D.14b (60 fps)
findings.finding: The 60 fps fixture is stated twice differently. The rule 'alpha_k = frac(k*TICK_RATE/fps), alpha_0 = 0' gives alpha_draw = 0, while the THEN clause and the running Example use a constant alpha_draw = 0.05. Both floor to S = -34 (-33.9 vs -33.75), so the oracle survives, but the fixture has two values.
findings.fix: State 0.05 as an explicit override for the 60 fps trace (the motion_latency example value), or use alpha = 0 and quote -33.9.

findings.section: D.14b f_q vs D.6b pose
findings.finding: f_q = floor(f_n/Q)*Q while the D.6b look-ahead-free pose is p + floor(d_n/Q)*Q with p = floor(target_n). They can differ by 1 base px (floor of a sum vs sum of floors), so 'cursor at picture centre gives cursor_world_aim = f_q exactly' places the aim up to 1 px from the picture-centre pixel on the D.6b path.
findings.fix: Note the 1 px tolerance in D.14b, or publish f_q = p + floor(d/Q)*Q when D.6b is the solver.

findings.section: D.12 Output Range / Edge Cases L821 / OQ 19
findings.finding: The text still asserts that the head is visible throughout a doorway crossing from either side, as fact, although it depends on door art not yet authored (OQ 19 hands this to the art-director).
findings.fix: Rephrase as 'holds if the art-director confirms the lintel/leaf constraint (OQ 19)'.

data.summary: Verdict: NEEDS REVISION, with one narrow BLOCKING item. The 2026-10-28 blocker (the mouse-aim 'exactly 32 px' oracle) is genuinely fixed. I re-derived lag_ss, the S fixtures at 60/90/144 fps, the bounds (36 run, 24 walk) and the Example arithmetic, and all agree. The Player Controller siblings mirror it, and no old wording survives. One new defect sits in the rewritten oracle: the AC checks S exactly after only 3*tau_eff (0.54 s), when about 1.5 px of lag is still unsettled. A correct implementation therefore gets S = -33 instead of -34 and fails an (auto) AC. The fix is to raise the settle time to about 10*tau (or relax the tolerance). The rest is carry-over RECOMMENDED material that this pass, which targeted blockers only, did not touch: the 'never twice per frame' promise is still false at walk and run speeds, D.6b is still a 'candidate' and its floor-then-clamp order contradicts D.8b, there is no entity_id namespace table, the CLAMPED aim mismatch is unbounded, several ACs lack evidence classes, the PR-15 keys are hard-coded to one wiring, spike steps 11-13 do not exist in the art bible, and counts, registry lists and two sibling GDDs (Web Map, Player Controller) are stale. Dependencies: 22 of 25 referenced GDDs exist; the missing ones (Settings, Accessibility, Failure Contract & Re-wake) are undesigned VS/Alpha systems and not blockers under R9. Everything else checked out: the D.3 expanded-field values, the D.15 fixtures, the P99 headroom arithmetic (14.9 ms / 30.0 ms) and the D.16 sum of 213 all re-compute correctly.
